title: libpod: reject startup healthcheck without a regular one on update
body:
`podman create` refuses a startup healthcheck if the container has no regular healthcheck (see `(*Container).validate()`), but `podman update` lets you add one anyway. Once a container is in that state, a later update of the startup healthcheck crashes podman:

```
$ podman run -d --name c alpine top
$ podman update --health-startup-cmd true c
$ podman restart -t0 c
$ podman update --health-startup-interval 5s c
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
[signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x28 pc=0x15af1c2]

goroutine 1 [running]:
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).recreateHealthCheckTimer(...)
	libpod/healthcheck.go:291 +0xa2
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).resetHealthCheckTimers(...)
	libpod/container_internal.go:2984 +0xe5
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).updateHealthCheck(...)
	libpod/container_internal.go:3021 +0x226
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).Update(...)
	libpod/container_api.go:149 +0x54f
```

After the restart `StartupHCPassed` is false again, so changing the interval goes through `resetHealthCheckTimers()` into `recreateHealthCheckTimer()`. That function reads `c.HealthCheckConfig().Interval` before it looks at `isStartup`, and `HealthCheckConfig` is nil here.

This PR does the same check in `Container.Update()` that creation does.

Found by Linux Verification Center (linuxtesting.org) with SVACE.
